newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals - Trade renews demand for duty relief.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals - Trade renews demand for duty relief.

text.p: India's non-ferrous metals sector will renew its demand for a cut in import duty on raw materials which currently attract the same rate as semi-finished products, traders said on Wednesday.
"We want a minimum diferential of 10-15 percent in duty on raw materials and semi-finished products," said Bombay Metals Exchange president Sharad Parikh.
Currently, the import duty on both raw materials and semi-finished items is 32 percent.
"User industries always prefer semi-finished goods to raw materials," Parikh said.
The federal budget for 1997/98 (April/March), presented to parliament on Friday by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram selectively gave duty reliefs to non-ferrous metals.

It halved import duty on nickel to 10 percent to help the domestic steel industry, where the former is a crucial component. The budget reduced import duty on tin to 20 percent from 30 percent to help the domestic alloys industry.
The budget provided relief to the aluminium industry, by raising import duty on aluminium ingots by 10 percent to 20 percent.
Analysts said the move is aimed at helping the domestic aluminium industry, which is saddled with high inventories.

"This will give additional price protection of 10 percent from imports to domestic units such as Hindustan Aluminium Co (Hindalco), National Aluminium Co (Nalco) and Madras Aluminium (Malco)," said one analyst.
The budget also reduced import duty on concentrates of copper and zinc to 5.0 percent from 10 percent to help domestic producers importing raw matrerials.
"But the budget failed to cut down import duty on copper and zinc," Parikh said.

In the week to Wednesday, copper gained 550 rupees and zinc rose 275 rupees per quintal on reduced imports. Tin came under pressure on fresh selling and lost 2,600 rupees to 31,500 rupees per quintal. Aluminium gained 150 rupees to 7,400 rupees per quintal and lead lost 25 rupees to 4,525.
